53084-a-manual-of-italian-literature.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. remote countries, is not wonderful; Carthage and Tyre did so at an earlier period, Venice and Genoa did so in times nearer the present; but that a solitary city should play a part reserved apparently only for a great nation, should draw to itself, as in a magic circle, all Italy, should conquer Gaul, Greece, Africa, Spain, Britain, Asia Minor, and even threaten Persia and India, is indeed marvellous.

58101-ragged-homes-and-how-to-mend-them.creator: Mrs Bayly.
58101-ragged-homes-and-how-to-mend-them.description: A book by Mrs Bayly.. AMIDST the excitements of political contests at home, with wars and rumours of wars abroad, the voice of “Social Science” is occasionally heard, and listened to, with a growing conviction of its importance. The Politician, the Moralist, and the Christian are impelled by various reasons to its consideration, and will listen with equal interest to its details.

arxiv-2109-11499.title: Cancellation mechanism of dark matter direct detection in Higgs-portal and vector-portal models
arxiv-2109-11499.creator: Chengfeng Cai, Yu-Pan Zeng, Hong-Hao Zhang
arxiv-2109-11499.description: Abstract We present two alternative proofs for the cancellation mechanism in the U(1) symmetric pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone-Boson Dark Matter (pNGB DM) model. They help us to have a better understanding of the mechanism from multi-angle, and inspire us to propose some interesting generalizations. In the first proof, we revisit the non-linear representation method and rephrase the argument with the interaction eigenstates.

arxiv-2203-00038.title: Entanglement based tomography to probe new macroscopic forces
arxiv-2203-00038.creator: Peter. F. Barker, Sougato Bose, Ryan J. Marshman, Anupam Mazumdar
arxiv-2203-00038.description: Abstract Quantum entanglement provides a novel way to test short distance physics in the non-relativistic regime. We will provide a protocol to potentially test new physics by bringing two charged massive particle interferometers adjacent to each other. Being charged, the two superpositions will be entangled via electromagnetic interactions mediated by the photons, including the Coulomb and the Casimir-Polder potential.

arxiv-2206-02598.title: [Reproducibility Report] Explainable Deep One-Class Classification
arxiv-2206-02598.creator: João P C Bertoldo, Etienne Decencière
arxiv-2206-02598.description: Abstract Reproducibility Summary Scope of Reproducibility Liznerski et al. [ 23 ] proposed Fully Convolutional Data Description (FCDD) , an explainable version of the Hypersphere Classifier (HSC) to directly address image anomaly detection (AD) and pixel-wise AD without any post-hoc explainer methods.

arxiv-2306-01271.title: On the Clean Generalization and Robust Overfitting in Adversarial Training from Two Theoretical Views: Representation Complexity and Training Dynamics
arxiv-2306-01271.creator: Binghui Li, Yuanzhi Li
arxiv-2306-01271.description: Abstract Similar to surprising performance in the standard deep learning, deep nets trained by adversarial training also generalize well for unseen clean data (natural data) . However, despite adversarial training can achieve low robust training error, there exists a significant robust generalization gap . We call this phenomenon the Clean Generalization and Robust Overfitting (CGRO) .

arxiv-2306-13913.title: Temporal Analysis of Misinformation on Parler
arxiv-2306-13913.creator: Eliana Norton, Thaïs Thomas, Akaash Kolluri, Torie Hyunsik Kim, Dhiraj Murthy
arxiv-2306-13913.description: Abstract Social media platforms have facilitated the rapid spread of dis- and mis-information. Parler, a US-based fringe social media platform that positions itself as a champion of free-speech, has had substantial information integrity issues. In this study, we seek to characterize temporal misinformation trends on Parler.

arxiv-2306-16222.title: The NANOGrav 15-year Data Set: Bayesian Limits on Gravitational Waves from Individual Supermassive Black Hole Binaries Facilities: Arecibo, GBT, VLA QuickCW ( Bécsy et al. 2023 ) , enterprise ( Ellis et al. 2019 ) , enterprise_extensions ( Taylor et al. 2021 ) , libstempo ( Vallisneri 2020 ) , tempo
arxiv-2306-16222.creator: Gabriella Agazie, Akash Anumarlapudi, Anne M. Archibald, Zaven Arzoumanian, Paul T. Baker, Bence Bécsy, Laura Blecha, Adam Brazier, Paul R. Brook, Sarah Burke-Spolaor, Robin Case, J. Andrew Casey-Clyde, Maria Charisi, Shami Chatterjee, Tyler Cohen, James M. Cordes, Neil J. Cornish, Fronefield Crawfo
arxiv-2306-16222.description: Abstract Evidence for a low-frequency stochastic gravitational wave background has recently been reported based on analyses of pulsar timing array data. The most likely source of such a background is a population of supermassive black hole binaries, the loudest of which may be individually detected in these datasets.

arxiv-2311-09929.title: Mutating etcd Towards Edge Suitability
arxiv-2311-09929.creator: Andrew Jeffery, Heidi Howard, Richard Mortier
arxiv-2311-09929.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Andrew Jeffery, Heidi Howard, Richard Mortier. In the edge environment servers are no longer being co-located away from clients, instead they are being co-located with clients away from other servers, focusing on reliable and performant operation. Orchestration platforms, such as Kubernetes , are a key system being transitioned to the edge but they remain unsuited to the environment, stemming primarily from their critical key-value stores.

arxiv-2404-12748.title: Moduli spaces of 3 3 -manifolds with boundary are finite
arxiv-2404-12748.creator: Rachael Boyd, Corey Bregman, Jan Steinebrunner
arxiv-2404-12748.description: Abstract . We study the classifying space B ​ Diff ⁡ ( M ) B\!\Diff(M) of the diffeomorphism group of a connected, compact, orientable 3-manifold M M . In the case that M M is reducible we build a contractible space parametrising the systems of reducing spheres.

arxiv-2407-12149.title: Multigrid Monte Carlo Revisited: Theory and Bayesian Inference
arxiv-2407-12149.creator: Yoshihito Kazashi, Eike Müller, Robert Scheichl
arxiv-2407-12149.description: Abstract Gaussian random fields play an important role in many areas of science and engineering. In practice, they are often simulated by sampling from a high-dimensional multivariate normal distribution, which arises from the discretisation of a suitable precision operator. Existing methods such as Cholesky factorization and Gibbs sampling become prohibitively expensive on fine meshes due to their high computational cost.

arxiv-2409-18417.title: VickreyFeedback: Cost-efficient Data Construction for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
arxiv-2409-18417.creator: Guoxi Zhang, Jiuding Duan 0
arxiv-2409-18417.description: Abstract This paper addresses the cost-efficiency aspect of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). RLHF leverages datasets of human preferences over outputs of llm ( llm )s to instill human expectations into llm s. Although preference annotation comes with a monetized cost, the economic utility of a preference dataset has not been considered by far.

arxiv-2411-12896.title: Nonradiative quenching of EPR signals in germanium-doped AlGaN: evidence for DX -center formation
arxiv-2411-12896.creator: Jason Forbus, Darshana Wickramaratne, John L. Lyons, M.E. Zvanut
arxiv-2411-12896.description: Abstract We present photo-electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) measurements and first-principles calculations that indicate germanium (Ge) is a DX center in AlGaN. Our photo-EPR measurements on Ge-doped AlGaN samples show no EPR spectra in the dark, while persistent EPR spectra is observed upon photoexcitation with photon energies greater than ∼ \sim 1.3 eV.

arxiv-2412-02555.title: Edge-based discretizations on triangulations in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , with special attention to four-dimensional space.
arxiv-2412-02555.creator: Nicholas Tufillaro, David M. Williams, Hiroaki Nishikawa, Tufillaro N, Williams D M, Nishikawa H
arxiv-2412-02555.description: Abstract Many time-dependent problems in the field of computational fluid dynamics can be solved using space-time methods. However, such methods can encounter issues with computational cost and robustness. In order to address these issues, efficient, node-centered edge-based schemes are currently being developed. In these schemes, a median-dual tessellation of the space-time domain is constructed based on an initial triangulation.

arxiv-2511-21338.title: Masks Can Be Distracting: On Context Comprehension in Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2511-21338.creator: Julianna Piskorz University of CambridgeCristina Pinneri, Qualcomm AI ResearchAlvaro Correia, Qualcomm AI ResearchMotasem Alfarra, Qualcomm AI ResearchRisheek Garrepalli, Qualcomm AI ResearchChristos LouizosQualcomm AI Research
arxiv-2511-21338.description: Abstract Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to Autoregressive Language Models (ARLMs), leveraging a denoising objective that, in principle, should enable more uniform context utilisation. In this work, we examine the context comprehension abilities of MDLMs and uncover two key limitations.

arxiv-2601-04865.title: Forming Invariant Stochastic Differential Systems with a Given First Integral
arxiv-2601-04865.creator: K. A. Rybakov
arxiv-2601-04865.description: Abstract Abstract. This article proposes a method for forming invariant stochastic differential systems, namely dynamic systems with trajectories belonging to a given smooth manifold. The Itô or Stratonovich stochastic differential equations with the Wiener component describe dynamic systems, and the manifold is implicitly defined by a differentiable function.

europmc-pmc6056715.title: Mitochondrial dynamics: overview of molecular mechanisms.
europmc-pmc6056715.creator: Tilokani L, Nagashima S, Paupe V, Prudent J.
europmc-pmc6056715.description: Mitochondria are highly dynamic organelles undergoing coordinated cycles of fission and fusion, referred as 'mitochondrial dynamics', in order to maintain their shape, distribution and size. Their transient and rapid morphological adaptations are crucial for many cellular...

pmc-10622455.title: A neurodegeneration checkpoint mediated by REST protects against the onset of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-10622455.creator: Liviu Aron, Chenxi Qiu, Zhen Kai Ngian, Marianna Liang, Derek Drake, Jaejoon Choi, Marty A. Fernandez, Perle Roche, Emma L. Bunting, Ella K. Lacey, Sara E. Hamplova, Monlan Yuan, Michael S. Wolfe, David A. Bennett, Eunjung A. Lee, Bruce A. Yankner
pmc-10622455.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Many aging individuals accumulate the pathology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) without evidence of cognitive decline. Here we describe an integrated neurodegeneration checkpoint response to early pathological changes that restricts further disease progression and preserves cognitive function. Checkpoint activation is mediated by the REST transcriptional repressor, which is induced in cognitively-intact aging humans and AD mouse models at the onset of amyloid β-protein (Aβ) deposition and tau accumulation. REST induction is mediated by the unfolded protein response together with β-catenin signaling.

pmc-12582274.title: Joint disruption of Ret and Ednrb transcription shifts cell fate trajectories in the enteric nervous system in Hirschsprung disease
pmc-12582274.creator: Ryan D. Fine, Rebecca Chubaryov, Mingzhou Fu, Gabriel Grullon, Aravinda Chakravarti
pmc-12582274.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SignificanceDespite the remarkable advancements in genetic mapping and the genomics of polygenic traits, the genetic mechanisms by which disease risk increases in individuals with genotypes bearing more risk variants than those with fewer remain unclear. We hypothesize disease penetrance arises as a result of the quantitative difference of the expression levels of rate-limiting core genes within larger interconnected gene regulatory networks. These rate-limiting genes have an expression threshold beyond which the cellular phenotype is altered and, thereby, the organismal phenotype as well.

pmc-12649216.title: Genomic Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Profile of Streptococcus uberis Strains Isolated from Cows with Mastitis from Northwestern Spain
pmc-12649216.creator: Emiliano J. Quinto, Paz Redondo del Río, Beatriz de Mateo Silleras, Alberto Prieto, Gonzalo López-Lorenzo, Carlos M. Franco, Beatriz I. Vázquez
pmc-12649216.description: Background/Objectives: Streptococcus uberis is a Gram-positive bacterium and a major cause of bovine mastitis. The use of antimicrobial treatments raises concerns about resistance. This study aimed to characterize S. uberis isolates from one of the ten largest milk-producing regions in Europe. Methods: Thirty-six isolates from 36 cows with mastitis were identified using MALDI-TOF and VITEK®MS.

pmc-12858326.title: Diagnostic Utility of Laparoscopy in Breast Cancer-Associated Carcinomatous Peritonitis With Suspected Advanced Ovarian Cancer
pmc-12858326.creator: Toshiya Nishimura, Hideaki Tsuyoshi, Fumikata Hara, Makoto Orisaka, Sayaka Fujiwara
pmc-12858326.description: Carcinomatous peritonitis (CP) secondary to breast cancer is an uncommon metastatic manifestation that presents considerable diagnostic challenges, particularly when the primary lesion is not detectable through imaging modalities. This report examines the case of a 54-year-old female patient who presented with abdominal pain and constipation.

pmc-13047402.title: Complication Analysis of Conversion Hip Arthroplasty after Failed Intertrochanteric Fracture Fixation: A Meta-Analysis
pmc-13047402.creator: Naye Kang, Ki-Tae Park, Suyeon Park, Eunseo Joung, Nah Yon Kim, Byung-Ho Yoon
pmc-13047402.description: BackgroundAlthough internal fixation (IF) techniques for intertrochanteric fractures have continuously advanced, the failure rate remains around 5%, often requiring secondary surgical intervention. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of conversion hip arthroplasty (CHA) following IF failure in intertrochanteric fracture patients.MethodsA total of 1,468 hips with CHA for failed IF of intertrochanteric fracture from 25 studies were included.

pmc-13076495.title: The impact of completion time on the reliability and validity of online electronic questionnaires: a preliminary study of the FABQ and ODI scales
pmc-13076495.creator: Shilin Bi, Chao Wang, Haowei Liu, Li Huang, Haodong Tian, Xing Zhang, Hansen Li
pmc-13076495.description: This study uses secondary analysis of a health survey dataset to explore the impact of completion time on the reliability and validity of online questionnaires. A total of 1,758 chronic low back pain patients recruited online were included in the study.

pmc-13106183.title: Distribution and antimicrobial resistance of pathogens in oral and maxillofacial infections during and Post-COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13106183.creator: Dandan Li, Zhujun Yu, Cheng Nie, Huamin Li, Jingjing Jiang, Jianli Wang
pmc-13106183.description: BackgroundThis study investigated the distribution characteristics and antimicrobial resistance patterns of pathogens isolated from patients with oral and maxillofacial infections during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed microbial cultures of specimens obtained from patients with odontogenic and non-odontogenic oral and maxillofacial infections during the pandemic period (January 2020–December 2022) and the post-pandemic period (January 2023–December 2024).

pmc-13224014.title: A novel approach to Roy-Camille type 2 sacral fracture: Percutaneous lumbopelvic fixation following manual hyperextension-assisted closed reduction
pmc-13224014.creator: Ali Güleç, Abdullah Balcı, Sadettin Çiftci, Ebubekir Eravsar, Selim Safalı, Bahattin Kerem Aydın
pmc-13224014.description: BackgroundTransverse sacral fractures with spinopelvic dissociation, commonly referred to as “suicidal jumper's fractures” -particularly Roy-Camille type 2 injuries- represent a rare and unstable injury pattern frequently associated with neurological deficits. Surgical management typically requires complex reduction maneuvers and rigid fixation to restore spinopelvic continuity and optimize functional outcomes.

pmc-13567340.title: Three-Dimensional Printed Materials for Definitive Ceramic and Resin Restorations: A Scoping Review
pmc-13567340.creator: Ioulianos Rachiotis, Aspasia Pachiou, Maurice Salem, Duygu Karasan, Irena Sailer, Christos Rahiotis
pmc-13567340.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: The integration of additive manufacturing (AM) into digital dentistry has extended 3D printing beyond auxiliary applications toward the fabrication of definitive restorations, yet the evidence remains dispersed across diverse materials and technologies. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence on 3D-printed resin- and ceramic-based materials for definitive tooth-supported restorations, including crowns, fixed dental prostheses, endocrowns, veneers, overlays, and onlays. Methods: The review followed the JBI framework and reported according to PRISMA-ScR.

pmc-13629398.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Single-Shot Plasma Emission Imaging for Pollen Morphology Reconstruction and Apparent Hydration-State Classification
pmc-13629398.creator: James A. Grant-Jacob, Yuchen Liu, Ben Mills
pmc-13629398.description: Monitoring pollen is important for crop productivity, plant breeding, and environmental forecasting, yet current approaches remain limited in throughput and physiological insight. Here, we combine single-shot plasma emission imaging with artificial intelligence for pollen morphology reconstruction and apparent hydration state classification. Plasma plumes generated during laser–pollen interaction provide indirect measurements of pollen morphology, extending plasma-based analysis beyond conventional spectroscopic readouts.

pmc-13679265.title: Stage-specific changes in schematic facial emotion recognition following childhood trauma: an ERP study
pmc-13679265.creator: Siyu Chen, Danmin Miao
pmc-13679265.description: BackgroundChildhood trauma has been linked to emotional face processing, but its association with stages of emotional face processing remains unclear. The present study used schematic emotional facial cues as simplified stimuli and event-related potentials to examine early face sensitive activity and later evaluative processing within this stimulus context.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter— (1) Agreed accounting standards The term “agreed accounting standards” means modified accrual accounting standards or, for any period during which the Oversight Board determines in its sole discretion that a territorial government is not reasonably capable.
